summary: One focused behavior: the 3D scene composition adapts to widescreen aspect ratios (21:9, 32:9) without letterboxed dead zones, per request section 16. The two named changed responsibilities (a pure-data widescreen layout params module in src/render/, and the existing camera transform seam applying the composition offsets) jointly deliver that single behavior and stay within the leaf limit; tests for them do not add responsibilities. Subsystem count is one concrete owner (camera - widescreen composition); 'baseline aspect ratios keep current framing' is a non-regression constraint of the same behavior, not a second one. Boundaries are explicit: HUD/overlay responsiveness, shake (WI-06d-c-a), juice (WI-06d-b), and geometry (WI-06d-a) are out of scope; no gameplay, steering, balance, or content changes. Frontmatter is well-formed; AC-widescreen is retained verbatim from parent WI-06d-c and this leaf is the story's named final proof owner; sibling WI-06d-c-a holds AC-shake-rules, so the children's union covers the parent. depends_on [WI-06a, WI-06b, WI-06c] exist under ST-06 and are inherited from the ancestor story, with no ancestor or descendant dependencies. Evidence is focused: Node unit tests for breakpoint-to-offset resolution and baseline invariance, plus a browser final proof at a wide aspect ratio (e.g. 21:9) in a settled band scene with a recorded wide-aspect capture, suite and build green. Handoff names the exact parent plans (WI-06d-c, WI-06d, ST-06), request section 16, and the camera transform code in src/render/, so a fresh implementer needs no full-task reconstruction.
